page: Amazon Web Services c7gd.12xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by custom AWS Graviton3 processors utilizing the ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 architecture. It features 48 dedicated physical cores running at 2.6 GHz with a single thread per core, backed by 96.0 GB of system memory, which provides 2.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance is built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and includes 2850 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage alongside a baseline network bandwidth of 22 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the c7gd.12xlarge demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities, scoring 73467.4 in stress-ng multi-core CPU tests and 19220.0 in Geekbench multi-core. Memory performance is highly competitive, with Passmark memory scores reaching the top tier and memory bandwidth tests showing strong read-only speeds of up to 4652.94 GB/sec for small cached blocks. Storage-related and transactional benchmarks are also notable, with Redis SET operations achieving a strong 76.38 million operations per second and static web serving throughput reaching 65.01 GB/sec.

While the instance exhibits strong performance in multi-threaded tasks, software compilation, and database operations, its single-core performance is moderate, as indicated by average scores in stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core tests. Additionally, text generation for small LLM models is relatively weak at 56.09 tokens per second, though medium-model text generation remains strong. Given its compute-focused resource density, local NVMe storage, and high memory bandwidth, the c7gd.12xlarge is well-suited for multi-threaded workloads, high-throughput database operations, static web serving, and software compilation.
description: Amazon Web Services c7gd.12xlarge is a compute-optimized, ARM64-based instance powered by an AWS Graviton Neoverse-V1 processor. It offers 48 dedicated physical cores running at 2.6 GHz, 96.0 GB of memory, and 2850 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 22 Gbps. Benchmarks indicate strong multi-core CPU performance, top-tier memory bandwidth, and high-throughput capabilities in database operations, Redis SET transactions, and static web serving. However, single-core CPU performance and small-model LLM text generation are more moderate. This instance is highly efficient for multi-threaded applications, high-performance databases, software compilation, and web serving workloads requiring fast local storage.
